newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV rates to rise 20 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV rates to rise 20 pct in Jan.

text.p: Venezuela's national telephone company CANTV will increase its rates an average of 20 percent from January 1, the company said.
According to a company release, the tariff increase is in line with the parameters approved by the Transport and Communications Ministry.
CANTV raises tariffs every quarter in line with inflation during the previous quarter. Tariffs were increased by an average of 21.31 percent in October.
Rates for local and long distance calls were raised but international calls remain unaltered, narrowing the cross-subsidy between the two.
CANTV currently has three plans for local calls of residential clients:
-- Under the "basic plan" the subscriber pays 1,558.70 bolivars ($3.30) per month and receives 60 pulses free. The cost of each additional pulse is 11.71 bolivars.
-- Under the "intermediate plan" the basic charge is 2,449.15 bolivars ($5.19) with 100 pulses free and each additional pulse costs 8.90 bolivars.
-- Under the "profitable plan" the basic charge is 4,030.90 bolivars ($8.54) with 150 free pulses and an additional cost of 6.90 bolivars pert pulse.
Non-residential lines cost 8,525.00 bolivars ($18.06) per month and charge 12.20 bolivars per pulse.

Under the new tariff structure operating from January long distance domestic calls will cost 8.25 bolivars per pulse for both residential and non-residential users with discounts of 50 percent available between 2100 and 0M59 local.
The rate increases do not affect international calls, the release said. International calls receive a 43 percent discount during off-peak hours.
CANTV said the new tariff increases "guarantee the plan of expansion and service improvement."
